items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1960-06-15
items.q: Well I got the set and my Uncle Clay taking me to Old Man Chaloner for lessons.

ctx.x: They were a lot cheaper then than them now.

Well I got the set and my Uncle Clay taking me to Old Man Chaloner for lessons. And Old Man Chaloner was a teacher. He didn't only teach you. He made you experience of learning to play instruments. He would have a big band of all of his scholars. On Monday you'd go to lessons. On Wednesday all his scholars would be in the band together. So he taking my Uncle Clay to play the bass drum to give the youngsters ideas about a band being so big. So they brought me over and I would play the snare drum. But they had…

items.title: Albert Jiles Interview, 1961-02-24
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] So your Uncle Clay now, did he play anything but street drums? [INTERVIEWEE] That's all he played, bass drums.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, he was a great drummer, one of your greatest drummers. But he played in orchestra with Piron. Well you see at those times that's how guys would play with two bands. Some guys didn't have a brass band but they had orchestra and they took practically to Goodman's for parades.
So your Uncle Clay now, did he play anything but street drums?
That's all he played, bass drums. He didn't even play trap drums.
